keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first shape begins in 1815 but the state begins on 6 April 1814. Treaty of Paris (1814) page, signed 30 May 1814: France kept 'Saarbrücken, Saarlouis, Landau, the County of Montbéliard, part of Savoy with Annecy and Chambéry' beyond its borders of 1 June 1792 (Montbéliard is already in the modern-France outline). Bouillon (annexed in 1795) is added from the Treaty of Paris (1815) page. Philippeville and Mariembourg, which the reviewer lists, are named on neither Treaty of Paris page and are not added. The Kotor stray is removed.

minus.text: a one-cell stray at 42.4 N 18.8 E (the Bay of Kotor) that Cliopatria's 1815-1819 shape carries

correction.text: the 1815 shape without the stray Kotor cell

keyframe_review.note: 628,140 km2 for 1815-1819: metropolitan France in its post-treaty frontiers ('its borders were reduced to those that had existed on 1 January 1790', keeping 'Comtat Venaissin, the County of Montbéliard, and the Republic of Mulhouse'), French Guiana, the Antilles and Senegal. One cell at 42.4 N 18.8 E (Bay of Kotor) lies far outside the 1790 frontier and no opened page gives it to France, so it is dropped. No infobox area on either France page; overseas holdings unverified: page budget. 'Until 1818, France was occupied by 1.2 million foreign soldiers' (Restoration page): the occupation is not drawn here (see notes).

629,073 km2 for 1820-1829: the same France after the occupation ended in 1818. No infobox area to compare. The Senegal and Ivory Coast cells (Grand-Bassam, 5.2 N 3.4 W) are unverified: page budget; no opened page mentions a French post on the Ivory Coast, so a gap-filler should check it. Repair run: the Grand-Bassam page says 'In 1843, after signing a treaty with the African ruler of the Grand-Bassam region, the French built Fort Memours' and mentions no earlier French presence, so the 1815-1841 Ivory Coast cells stay unverified (they may be older posts such as Assinie, which no opened page confirms).

629,044 km2 for 1830-1833: July Revolution of 26-29 July 1830 and the monarchy of 9 August 1830 change the regime, not the frontier. Algiers is French Algeria's (separate dossier). Unverified overseas cells: page budget.

629,026 km2 for 1834-1835: no border change on the pages. The 1834 annexation of the occupied part of Algeria (conquest page: 'On 22 June 1834, France formally annexed the occupied areas of Algeria') belongs to french-algeria, not to this shape.
629,311 km2 for 1836-1839: unchanged metropolitan France. The Tlemcen and Constantine campaigns are Algerian, carried by french-algeria and emirate-of-abdelkader.

correction.text: the 1842 shape without the Gabon coast, which is a French protectorate (ledger vassal_start 1838)

keyframe_review.note: 644,966 km2 for 1842-1845, about 16,000 km2 (31 cells) more than the 1840 shape: the extra cells are Gabon coast that the other shapes lack. The Gabon page: 'In 1838 and 1841, France established a protectorate over the coastal regions of Gabon', so the coast is a protectorate (lighter tint, rule 4), not direct land; the cells are removed here and drawn through the vassal events of the ledger.

625,552 km2 for 1846-1847: unchanged metropolitan France; the shape has no African cells at all, so Senegal and the Gabon coast that the 1815-1845 shapes carry are missing. Unverified: page budget (the Gabon page shows the protectorate continuing: Libreville is founded after 1849). Gap for a filler.

correction.text: the 1846-1847 outline, for 1848 up to the February Revolution

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the July Monarchy lasts to 24 February 1848 but Cliopatria's row ends in 1847. The shape is the 1846 outline, for the final year.

ledger.note: 6 April 1814: the Bourbons are restored in France. 'The first Bourbon Restoration lasted from 6 April 1814 to 20 March 1815.' Napoleon had been offered the throne in February 1814 on condition that 'France return to its 1792 frontiers'; the Treaty of Paris (1815) page confirms the 1814 treaty left 1792 frontiers. Region is the researcher's reading (France within 1792 frontiers).

region.text: the part of Savoy with Annecy and Chambéry that France kept in 1814

ledger.note: Treaty of Paris (1814) page: France retained 'Saarbrücken, Saarlouis, Landau, the County of Montbéliard, part of Savoy with Annecy and Chambéry'. The Treaty of Paris (1815) page names no Savoy cession (it mentions Savoy only as something Prussia 'adamantly demanded'), so the loss is a bridge over that silence: France is reduced to its 1 January 1790 frontiers and kingdom-of-sardinia records the gain (ledger/29, confidence 1). Year only.

20 November 1815: the Second Treaty of Paris takes 'Landau and the Saarlouis exclave, which had been French since 1697' (Treaty of Paris (1815) page, which names no recipient). Landau page: 'Landau, which had remained French, was granted to the Kingdom of Bavaria in 1815.' kingdom-of-bavaria's dossier records the Palatinate exchange with austrian-empire in April 1816 (/14); the Landau page does not mention Austria, so the recipient follows the page and the month follows the treaty.

region.text: the former duchy of Bouillon, annexed to France in 1795

ledger.note: 20 November 1815: 'The former duchy of Bouillon, annexed to France in 1795' is ceded (Treaty of Paris (1815) page). Duchy of Bouillon page: under the Treaty of Paris of 1815 'the sovereignty of the former duchy was attributed to the king of Netherlands as grand duke of Luxemburg'. The counterpart is the king's state, netherlands (netherlands/ledger/2 records the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg as its vassal).

Saarlouis page: 'With the Treaty of Paris in 1815, Saarlouis (and the whole region later known as the Saargebiet) became Prussian.' The Treaty of Paris (1815) page lists the Saarlouis exclave among the losses without a recipient and does not mention Saarbrücken (the Treaty of Paris (1814) page has France keeping it), so Saarbrücken is read as part of the Saargebiet. Month from the treaty (20 November 1815).

region.text: six communes in the Pays de Gex

ledger.note: 20 November 1815: six communes of the Pays de Gex go to Geneva. 'Six communes in the Pays de Gex, which were ceded to the Canton of Geneva' so that Geneva could be connected to the rest of Switzerland; swiss-confederation records the gain.

region.text: 'in the eastern border territories of France, from the English Channel to the border with Switzerland'

ledger.counterpart: Seventh Coalition army of occupation (austrian-empire, kingdom-of-prussia, russian-empire and British forces)
ledger.note: 20 November 1815, Second Treaty of Paris: 'parts of France were to be occupied by up to 150,000 soldiers for five years, with France covering the cost', 'in the eastern border territories of France, from the English Channel to the border with Switzerland'. The page gives the treaty date and no separate start date for the occupation. The page names no departments: the eleven border departments from Nord to Doubs (Pas-de-Calais for the Channel end) are my reading of its words, and the Restoration page's 'Until 1818, France was occupied by 1.2 million foreign soldiers' counts the whole occupation. The counterpart is free text because the occupiers were an allied army, not one state; none of austrian-empire, kingdom-of-prussia or russian-empire carries the roles-reversed event. Recorded here because the schema makes the owner of the land record the same event with the roles reversed.

region.text: 'in the eastern border territories of France, from the English Channel to the border with Switzerland'

ledger.counterpart: Seventh Coalition army of occupation (austrian-empire, kingdom-of-prussia, russian-empire and British forces)
ledger.note: 1818: 'the foreign troops withdrew from France in 1818' (Treaty of Paris (1815) page); the Restoration page agrees ('Until 1818'). No month on either page.

region.text: Spain, entered by the French army on 7 April 1823; the page names no occupied districts

ledger.note: 7 April 1823: 'the "100,000 Sons of Saint Louis" under the Duke of Angoulême entered Spain without opposition'; Cádiz surrendered on 30 September and the army left 'an occupying force of 45,000 men under the command of Bourmont'. The region is the whole kingdom because the page names no occupied districts; the area really held was smaller and shrank as 'Spain was then progressively evacuated', so a renderer should treat it as approximate. The Restoration page's infobox dates the invasion 6 April 1823; kingdom-of-spain's ledger has no mirror (not this batch's file).
1828: 'Spain was then progressively evacuated, but the French withdrawal was fully completed only in 1828.' No month on the page.

14 June 1830: French troops land at Sidi Ferruch. 'General de Bourmont then landed 34,000 soldiers 27 kilometres west of Algiers, at Sidi Ferruch, on 14 June 1830'; the conquest 'began in the last days of the Bourbon Restoration by Charles X'.
5 July 1830: Algiers falls. The French 'entered Algiers on 5 July after a three-week campaign'; french-algeria records its founding from this surrender.

9 August 1830: the House of Orléans replaces the Bourbons as Louis Philippe becomes King of the French. July Monarchy page: monarchy established 9 August 1830 after the July Revolution of 26-29 July; Restoration page: he ruled 'not as King of France but as King of the French'.

15 November 1832: the Siege of Antwerp page's infobox dates the operation '15 November - 23 December 1832' and says the marshal 'returned with his army to Belgium November 15, 1832, when he laid siege to Antwerp'. The page gives no separate date for the opening of the citadel siege. Replaces the earlier year-only entry at confidence 1; the netherlands dossier has no mirror contest.
23 December 1832: the Antwerp citadel capitulates. 'taking back the citadel of Antwerp, which capitulated on 23 December 1832'; the citadel passes to Belgium, not France.
January 1836: Clauzel occupies Tlemcen. 'In January 1836 Clausel occupied Tlemcen.' The Desmichels treaty of 1834 had brought a truce; emirate-of-abdelkader records the same start.

region.text: the Oran country ceded to Abdelkader's emirate and the French coastal posts

ledger.note: May 1837: the Treaty of Tafna. 'In May 1837, General Thomas Robert Bugeaud' negotiated it; the page gives no day (emirate-of-abdelkader has 30 May 1837 from its own page).

1838: France establishes a protectorate over the coast of Gabon. 'In 1838 and 1841, France established a protectorate over the coastal regions of Gabon.' The page does not say which treaty covered which coast; 1838 is the first year, 1841 the second.

region.text: the Iron Gates and the Mitidja, then all of Abdelkader's country

ledger.note: Late 1839: the war with Abdelkader resumes. 'When French troops contested this claim in late 1839 by marching through a mountain defile known as the Iron Gates' and 'In 1839 he launched the Mitidja Campaign'; 'Valée's failures to end the war led to his replacement in December 1840 by General Bugeaud.' Zone is the researcher's reading; emirate-of-abdelkader records the same restart.

13 March 1844: 'the Tahitian populace began an armed resistance on 13 March 1844'; the first battle the page names is Mahaena, 17 April 1844. Mirrors kingdom-of-tahiti ledger/3 (contest_start 1844-3).

17 December 1846: 'the capture of Fort Fautaua' ended the guerrilla conflict; 'In February 1847, Queen Pōmare IV returned from her exile and acquiesced to rule under the protectorate.' Mirrors kingdom-of-tahiti ledger/4 (contest_end 1846-12).

December 1847: Abdelkader surrenders. 'in December 1847, Abd al-Qādir chose to surrender to the French.' emirate-of-abdelkader ends the contest in 1846 (the Kabylia campaign of 1845-1846); the conquest page's infobox gives the war as '1830-1847'.

1848: the Gabon protectorate passes to the Second Republic. Page silent: nothing opened dates an end of the protectorate; the event closes the pair at the state's own end, and the relation continues under french-second-republic (Libreville is founded after 1849, Gabon page).

24 February 1848: the July Monarchy falls to the February Revolution. Infobox: monarchy ended 24 February 1848 'with the Revolution of 1848'; Louis-Philippe 'abdicated following the successful February Revolution'. french-second-republic records its founding that day.

wars.name: Hundred Days
wars.outcome: 'Napoleon, on 20 March 1815, returned to Paris from Elba'; 'On 8 July 1815 the kingdom was restored'. The Second Treaty of Paris (20 November 1815) reduced France to its 1790 frontiers.
wars.note: The state is recorded as continuous: the legitimist kingdom was 'restored' on 8 July 1815. The Restoration page names no battles.

wars.name: French intervention in Spain (Hundred Thousand Sons of Saint Louis)
wars.outcome: 'On 7 April, the "100,000 Sons of Saint Louis" under the Duke of Angoulême entered Spain without opposition'; Fort Trocadero was assaulted on 31 August, 'On 30 September Cádiz surrendered', 'The French army fired its last shots in Spain at the start of November', 'leaving behind an occupying force of 45,000 men'; 'the French withdrawal was fully completed only in 1828'.
wars.note: The Restoration page's infobox dates the invasion 6 April 1823; the Hundred Thousand Sons page gives 7 April for the entry (its infobox reads 18 April - 23 November 1823). No French territorial gain; the occupation to 1828 is in the ledger.

wars.name: French conquest of Algeria

zones.text: the Regency of Algiers and Abdelkader's emirate

wars.outcome: 'French victory' (infobox 1830-1847): landing 14 June 1830, Algiers 5 July 1830, annexation of the occupied areas 22 June 1834, Abdelkader's surrender in December 1847.
wars.note: Algeria is not in this dossier's shapes: french-algeria (1830-1847) holds it. The contests here mirror emirate-of-abdelkader's and regency-of-algiers's ledgers.

wars.name: Belgian Revolution (French intervention at Antwerp)
wars.outcome: William I's invasion of Belgium 'on 2 August 1831' brought French help; 'Marshal Gérard assisted the young Belgian monarchy with 70,000 men, taking back the citadel of Antwerp, which capitulated on 23 December 1832'.
wars.note: No French territorial gain; the citadel goes to Belgium. The Siege of Antwerp (1832) page dates the French operation 15 November - 23 December 1832 (infobox) and says the siege 'ended on 23 December 1832'.

wars.name: Franco-Tahitian War
wars.outcome: 'French victory' (infobox 1844-1847): armed resistance from 13 March 1844, Mahaena 17 April 1844, Fort Fautaua captured 17 December 1846; 'In February 1847, Queen Pōmare IV returned from her exile and acquiesced to rule under the protectorate.'
wars.note: The lead calls it a war between 'the Kingdom of France and the Kingdom of Tahiti and its allies'; the contest events in the ledger mirror kingdom-of-tahiti.

certainty.note: Metropolitan frontiers are treaty lines (the 1814 treaty, then 1 January 1790 after 20 November 1815); the overseas cells (Senegal, Guiana, the Antilles, the Gabon coast) are approximate and should be drawn soft.

notes: Written from five pages (budget up to 5); the repair run opened nine more. One state or two? Cliopatria's 'Bourbon Kingdom of France' (1815-1847) shares Wikidata Q207162 with 'Kingdom of France' (987-1791), whose dossier ends on 21 September 1792 with a dissolve into french-first-republic and says the merge, if any, belongs here. This dossier treats them as DIFFERENT states: twenty-one years of republic, consulate and empire (french-first-republic, french-directory, french-consulate, first-french-empire) separate them, and the Restoration page treats the July Monarchy as a successor regime, not a continuation. They share the colour family france. No predecessor link to kingdom-of-france is made. The July Monarchy (1830-1848) stays inside this state as a rename (Bourbon to Orléans, 9 August 1830), per rule 2: same land, no break. Cliopatria's row ends 1847; the state is dated to 24 February 1848 (new keyframe 1848). Cliopatria's shapes are metropolitan France, French Guiana, the Antilles and Senegal, with strays: a one-cell fragment at the Bay of Kotor in 1815-1819 (removed), Ivory Coast cells at 5.2 N 3.4 W in 1815-1841 and Gabon coast cells in 1842-1845 (removed and drawn as a protectorate), and no African cells in 1846-1847. Savoy and Nice are not in the shapes (probed). Added in the repair run (2026-11-01, pages re-opened): the allied occupation of north-eastern France, 1815-11 to 1818 (the owner of the land records it, counterpart the coalition as free text; the earlier remark here that 'occupation events belong to the occupiers' was wrong, the schema has the owner record the same event with the roles reversed); the 1823 intervention in Spain with its occupation to 1828; the Franco-Tahitian War contest 1844-3 to 1846-12 (mirrors kingdom-of-tahiti); the Antwerp contest start (15 November 1832, confidence 3); the recipients of Saarlouis and Saarbrücken (kingdom-of-prussia), Landau (kingdom-of-bavaria, per the Landau page; kingdom-of-bavaria's dossier has it via austrian-empire in 1816) and Bouillon (netherlands); the loss of Annecy-Chambéry to kingdom-of-sardinia at confidence 1 (the Treaty of Paris (1815) page is silent on Savoy). Still not in the ledger: Philippeville and Mariembourg (on neither Treaty of Paris page); French holdings in Senegal, Guiana, the Antilles, Réunion, India and Oceania other than Tahiti (french-india, french-colony-of-guiana and others); the end of the Gabon protectorate (the French Gabon page has no coastal treaty dates, the vassal_end stays at confidence 1); Senegal in the 1846-1847 shape and the Ivory Coast cells of 1815-1841 (Grand-Bassam page: post built 1843, nothing earlier). Not in kingdom-of-spain's or the netherlands' ledgers: mirrors of the 1823 occupation and the 1832 Antwerp contest. Abdelkader: this ledger ends the contest in December 1847 (surrender, conquest page); emirate-of-abdelkader ends it in 1846. The 1832 Antwerp contest start is year-only at confidence 1. Gazetteer names needed: places Landau (Germany), Saarlouis, Bouillon (Belgium), Gex. Area: neither France page gives an infobox area, so no area ratio is computed.
